 Search Go Entertainment The search for the next James Bond narrows
 After years of speculation and a revolving door of rumored contenders, the search for Daniel Craig’s successor is narrowing to a handful of actors — and Pierce Brosnan recently weighed in on a possible 007
 Published: Nov 3, 2026, 9:45 a.m. MST Updated: Nov 4, 2026, 10:58 a.m. MST See More Deseret News Stories In Search View 4 Comments Share Daniel Craig appears at the premiere of the film "No Time To Die" in London on Sept. 28, 2021. Matt Dunham, Associated Press By Margaret Darby Margaret is a staff writer for the Deseret News, where she covers entertainment, culture and trending topics.  Almost all the pieces for the next Bond film are firmly in place. For nearly a year, “Dune” filmmaker Denis Villeneuve has been attached to direct. And Steven Knight, the screenwriter behind “Peaky Blinders,” is set to write the script, with producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman also on board. 
 It leaves one final missing piece: Who will play 007? 
 As it stands, four actors reportedly remain in contention — Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and one unnamed actor. 
 Screen tests for the role have been underway for the final group of actors, according to The Guardian . The process is said to last roughly a week and includes three elements: screen presence, stunts and dialogue. 
 It marks the first major Bond screen test in more than 20 years, when Daniel Craig ultimately landed the role of the British secret service agent. Now, four years after Craig’s departure, following an acclaimed 15-year stint as 007, the search for his successor continues. 
 “We are being really, really methodical,” Pascal recently told Deadline . “I mean, Daniel Craig is a hard act to follow. And it’s got to be something (that is) stirring, and exciting, and different.”
 The ongoing hunt for the next Bond has fed years of speculation. 
 Dozens of names have been spat out by the rumor mill, with seemingly every young British actor linked to the role at one point or another. The list of contenders has included Idris Elba, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Jack O’Connell, Theo James, Jonathan Bailey, James Norton and Tom Hardy. 
 Tom Holland, Harris Dickinson, Henry Cavill, Paul Mescal and Jacob Elordi have also been mentioned. 
 Elba led the pack during the early stages of the hunt. His name was eventually crossed out and replaced by Taylor-Johnson, who emerged as the strongest candidate before the 007 search recently narrowed. 
 While the rumor mill has produced no shortage of candidates, the latest reports suggest the field is finally narrowing — bringing audiences closer to learning who will inherit the role, with three actors at the center of the speculation. 
 Related Opinion: James Bond’s forgotten moral code The hunt for the next James Bond continues. It’s a 10-year commitment The Bond shortlist
 Jack Lowden 
 Jack Lowden, a 36-year-old Scottish actor, has stayed guarded about speculation linking him to the role. 
 In a recent interview with British GQ , Lowden addressed casting rumors, describing the speculation as “very flattering.” 
 “It’s nice to be mentioned — for any role — and I’m just not really going to add to the noise,” he added. 
 Jack Lowden arrives at the 82nd Golden Globes on Sunday, Jan. 5, 2025, at the Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills, Calif. | Jordan Strauss, Associated Press Last month, his “Slow Horses” co-star Gary Oldman told Canada’s “ The Morning Show ” that he has his “fingers crossed” that Lowden would get the 007 role. 
 When asked about Oldman’s comment, Lowden responded, “It’s very nice, and Gary’s a sweetheart — it’s particularly lovely, coming from someone like him. But I don’t really listen to it.”
 He added, “As a young male actor, generally, the minute you’re not playing a zany artist type, the minute you’re in a suit, people fling it at you.”
 Lowden has earned two Emmy nominations for his portrayal of River Cartwright, an ambitious MI5 agent, in “Slow Horses.” His other credits include “Dunkirk,” “Mary Queen of Scots” and “Ella McCay.” He is also set to play Mr. Darcy in Netflix’s upcoming “Pride and Prejudice” miniseries. 
 Callum Turner
 Callum Turner, also 36, is another leading contender for 007. 
 “I know as much as you do — really, I know as much as you do,” Turner told The Hollywood Reporter in June, when asked about the Bond rumors. “I’m not going to comment on that.”
 “I’ll tell you what’s so funny about the Bond thing: Even your best friends ask you, people text you that you haven’t spoken to for 10 years — and you know nothing!” he added. 
 Callum Turner attends the premiere of "One Night Only" at the SVA Theatre on Monday, Aug. 3, 2026, in New York. | Charles Sykes, Associated Press Amid growing Bond speculation, he reportedly recently stepped down this month as a director of Twentytwo Films Ltd., a production company he co-founded last year with his wife Dua Lipa, per Esquire . 
 The timing adds another layer to the speculation, although there is no indication that the move is connected to the Bond role. 
 The British actor boasts a diverse list of credits, showing his versatility across projects including “The Boys in the Boat,” “Masters of the Air,” “Eternity,” “Green Room,” “Emma.” and “The Fantastic Beasts” franchise. 
 Josh O’Connor
 Josh O’Connor is another name reportedly in contention for 007. 
 The 36-year-old British actor previously addressed Bond rumors in an interview with Deadline in January 2025, when he found himself swept up in speculation after joking about how it would be funny if he played the MI6 agent. 
 Josh O'Connor, left and Alana Haim pose for photographers upon arrival at the premiere of the film 'The Mastermind' at the 78th international film festival, Cannes, southern France, Friday, May 23, 2025. | Scott A Garfitt, Associated Press “I have no thoughts, really,” he told Deadline . “The truth is that … I think in the space of a week, I made a joke about, wouldn’t it be funny if I played Bond? Then, me and Daniel (Craig) did an Actors on Actors, and then something else happened, and then suddenly I was James Bond.”
 He added, “If I am Bond, I don’t know about it.”
 O’Connor has earned acclaim for his performances in “The Crown,” for which he won an Emmy for playing Prince Charles, as well as “Challengers,” “Disclosure Day,” “God’s Own Country,” “The Mastermind” and “The History of Sound.” 
 Related Dick Van Dyke almost played James Bond — here’s why he said no A history of one of the most popular and widely recognized characters in cinema: James Bond Pierce Brosnan weighs in 
 Former 007 Pierce Brosnan is among those “eagerly” awaiting news of the next Bond actor. 
 Brosnan, who played the MI6 spy across four film, said he respects all the Bond contenders, but gave an especially warm endorsement to Turner, who played his troubled son in the 2017 film “The Only Living Boy in New York.” 
 “All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire. Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong,” Brosnan told Vanity Fair on Tuesday. “They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men.”
 “Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage,” he continued. “You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond.” 
 In terms of director Villeneuve’s vision for the Bond franchise, Brosnan says: “I think we are going to be blown away.”
 “(Villeneuve) is such an iconoclastic director,” he continued. “His work is visionary, and his stealth and imagination of camera work and storytelling is so visceral and sensuous. It’s going to be great. It’s going to be truly magnificent.”
 What else do we know about the next ‘James Bond’?
 The long-serving creative and operational brains behind the “James Bond” franchise, Barbara Broccoli and Michael G Wilson, relinquished control to Amazon MGM studios in early 2025. 
 As part of the new venture, the pair “ remain co-owners of the franchise ,” though they gave complete creative control to Amazon MGM Studios, meaning the upcoming Bond reboot will bring the first film made without the Broccoli dynasty calling the creative shots. 
 “Since his theatrical introduction over 60 years ago, James Bond has been one of the most iconic characters in filmed entertainment,” said Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios. 
 “We are honoured to continue this treasured heritage, and look forward to ushering in the next phase of the legendary 007 for audiences around the world.”
 4 Comments There is no timeline for when the official decision for the next Bond will be announced, though the film is positioned to be released sometime in 2028. 
 “I know you’re all wondering when we’re going to announce who’s playing James Bond,” said Courtenay Valenti, Amazon MGM’s head of film, in April, per The Guardian . “Don’t get too excited. Please know that we’re taking the time to do this with care and deep respect. It is the dream of a lifetime for all of us to bring audiences this next chapter, and it’s a responsibility we don’t take lightly.”
 “What I can tell you is this: when you pair one of the most beloved franchises in history with a world-class film-making team, including the brilliant director Denis Villeneuve, extraordinary producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman, executive producer Tanya Lapointe and screenwriter Steven Knight, you’re setting the stage for something that’s truly worthy of the Bond legacy.”
 She concluded, “That film is coming, and when the time is right, we’ll have much more to share.”
